o.text: Internationalism. Borrowed from Russian ию́ль (ijúlʹ), from Medieval Greek Ἰούλιος (Ioúlios), ultimately from Latin iūlius.

Inherited from Proto-Turkic *köŋül (“heart, mood”). Cognate with Turkish gönül.
Further cognates
Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰚𐰇𐰭𐰠 (köŋül), Crimean Tatar göñül or köñül (Northern Dialect), Turkmen göwün, Gagauz gön, Uzbek koʻngil, Uyghur كۆڭۈل (kö'ngül), Bashkir and Tatar күңел (küñel), Kazakh көңіл (köŋil), Yakut көҥүл (köŋül, “will, freedom”), Dolgan көҥүл (“permission”), Chuvash кӑмӑл (kămăl).

Borrowed from Persian بازوبند (bâzu-band).
Equivalent to bazu + bənd.
From Proto-Turkic *yïlïg. Cognate with Turkish ılık, Turkmen ýyly, Uzbek iliq, Bashkir йылы (yılı), etc.
From Armenian տղա (tġa), ultimately from Classical Syriac ܛܠܝܐ (ṭalyāʼ, “boy”).
